name: Candyland Slab
_identity: SLOW IS THE FLEX. Two tons of underdamped land yacht: springs 36000 at 0.32 of critical, so the body breathes over every crest and settles in three bounces instead of one. The rack is the slowest in the fleet (steer_speed 3.6, 31 deg lock) and the falloff is deliberately LOW (0.020) so it keeps steering at speed -- the car floats, it does not calm down. Rear-drive on 1.02 tires with lateral_stiffness 7200 means the back end goes early, goes gently, and goes a long way; angular_damp 0.28 lets the slide hold instead of snapping back. Measured M16: the slowest launch (6.58 s to 20 m/s), the laziest yaw (47.0 deg/s at full lock = a 12.6 m circle where the cruiser turns in 7.7), and it holds the most speed through that corner because it is sliding, not gripping. It cannot out-run anything and is not trying to.
_tuning_math: corner mass = 2050/4 = 512.5 kg; static load = 512.5*9.81 = 5027.6 N; spring_rate 36000 N/m -> static compression = 5027.6/36000 = 0.1396 m = 31.7% of suspension_rest 0.44 (deliberately past the 20-30% target: visible weight transfer is the look); critical damping = 2*sqrt(36000*512.5) = 8590 N*s/m; damping 2750 = 0.32 * critical -- underdamped on purpose. hardpoint (-0.30) sits below CoM (-0.22) so lateral tire forces roll the body OUT of corners on a 0.08 m lever: lazy lean, never scary. Ride: pivot at -0.30-(0.44-0.1396) = -0.600, wheel radius 0.34 -> ground at -0.940, i.e. 0.028 m LOWER than the M10 setup and 0.06*h of rocker skirt now reaches for it. Rollover check: CoM 0.720 m above ground vs half-track 0.900 m -> tips at ~1.25 g, tires only supply 1.02 g, so it ALWAYS slides before it rolls. Rear-drive traction limit: rear axle carries (1.68-0.10)/3.46 = 45.7% of 2050 kg = 9182 N, x1.02 = 9366 N against 17500 N of engine -- launches are pure wheelspin at ~4.6 m/s^2 and the throttle is a steering input.
_track_change_cycle2: TRACK 1.65 -> 1.80 (D-021). The bodywork stood 55.0 mm outboard of its own tyre at arch height: the arch lip could not reach the bar however it was capped, AND the flank buried the wheel it was supposed to open onto. Two levers exist -- bring the hull in, or widen the track -- and the builder's BEAM_INSET now guarantees the first for the whole fleet. Taken alone it would have cost the Slab 96 mm of beam inside a 2.0 m collider it is supposed to fill, leaving the widest, lowest car in the game narrower over its tyres than the police sedan. So the track carries this one instead: at 1.80 the tyre face reaches 1.020 and the clamp barely bites (2 mm), the shell keeps its full 2.0 m beam, and the wheels sit at the corners -- which is the whole visual thesis of a slab. HANDLING CONSEQUENCE, stated per the producer's condition. Roll stiffness scales with track^2: +9.1% track = +19.0% roll stiffness, and steady-state lean at 1 g falls 0.94 -> 0.79 deg. That lean is set by the 0.08 m hardpoint-to-CoM lever, not by the track, which is why the whole change is 0.15 deg on a car that was already leaning less than a degree -- it is arithmetic, not a feel change. Lateral load transfer m*a*h/t drops 8.3%, so the inside tyre unloads slightly less. Rollover margin moves the SAFE way: 1.145 -> 1.250 g against 1.02 g of tyre, so it still ALWAYS slides before it rolls, which is the D-012 check as written. UNTOUCHED: mass, engine, brakes, top speed, steer lock/speed/falloff, spring rate, damping, lateral_stiffness, handbrake mult, angular_damp, drag, CoM, wheelbase. Launch, braking, yaw rate and turn circle are arithmetically identical -- none of them contains track. The float (36000 N/m at 0.32 of critical) is the identity and it is not touched at all.
